title: Java Scope
learningObjectives: Define scope as the region of code where a variable can be accessed.
Distinguish local variables from class-level fields.
Explain block scope for variables declared inside braces.
Recognize that a local variable must be initialized before it is read.
Use clear variable names and narrow scopes to reduce unintended access.

understand.concept: Scope determines where a variable name is visible and can be used. A local variable belongs to the method or block where it is declared. A field belongs to an object or class and can be accessed by methods according to its access and static rules.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding scope prevents accidental use of the wrong variable and helps keep data limited to the code that needs it. Narrow scopes make programs easier to reason about and maintain.
understand.analogy: Think of a method as a named tool: give it the information it needs, let it perform one defined task, and use its result when appropriate.
understand.analogyLimit: A program follows exact language rules; a real-world tool may need judgment and safety checks that code must model explicitly.

explain.narrative:
## Local variables

A variable declared inside a method is local to that method. It cannot be accessed directly from another method. Local variables must be assigned before they are read.

## Block scope

Variables declared inside a block, such as an `if` or `for` body, are available only within that block and its nested blocks. The name can be reused in a separate, non-overlapping block when Java's declaration rules allow it.

## Fields

A field is declared in a class but outside its methods. Instance fields belong to objects; static fields belong to the class. Fields receive default values when not explicitly initialized, unlike local variables.

## Common mistakes

- Trying to use a local variable after its block ends.
- Reading a local variable before assigning it.
- Confusing a field with a local variable that has the same name.
- Declaring a local variable in a scope where the same name is already declared.

questions.explanation: Local variables belong to the method or block where they are declared.

questions.prompt: When can a local variable be read?
questions.answer: After it has definitely been assigned
options: After it has definitely been assigned

questions.prompt: What happens to a variable declared inside a for loop's initializer?
questions.answer: Its scope is limited to that for statement and body
options: Its scope is limited to that for statement and body
It is available in every method
